cause: Pre-existing fork defect (backlog B102) from fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 [LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms: PULPFixupHwLoops ('hwloopsfixup') was registered only from its constructor, never in LLVMInitializeRISCVTarget, so llc's -run-pass/-stop-before/-stop-after/-start-before/-start-after lookups failed with 'pass is not registered' (logs/20-F032.repro.log).
fix: RISCV.h: declare void initializePULPFixupHwLoopsPass(PassRegistry &); RISCVTargetMachine.cpp: call initializePULPFixupHwLoopsPass(*PR) in LLVMInitializeRISCVTarget after initializePULPHardwareLoopsPass. Same pattern as all upstream RISC-V passes (RISCVTargetMachine.cpp:120-146 @llvmorg-20.1.8). PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp (owned by F025) NOT edited: its INITIALIZE_PASS name 'hwloopsfixup' and duplicate llvm-namespace declaration are compatible, no change needed there.
other_passes_checked: All INITIALIZE_PASS in llvm/lib/Target/RISCV compared against LLVMInitializeRISCVTarget: fork passes PULPExpandPseudo, PULPHardwareLoops, RISCVExpandSSR, RISCVExpandSDMA, SNITCHFrepLoops already registered; only PULPFixupHwLoops was missing. (Upstream-only RISCVExpandAtomicPseudo, RISCVLandingPadSetup, RISCVRedundantCopyElimination, RISCVZacasABIFix are also unregistered, same as upstream llvmorg-20.1.8; not touched.)

other_errors_seen: -start-after=hwloopsfixup (and generally resuming from MIR after pulp-hwloops/hwloopsfixup/frep) yields asm that does not assemble: 'Undefined temporary symbol .LBB0_3'. The MIR format at llvmorg-20.1.8 does not serialize MachineBasicBlock::LabelMustBeEmitted, which the fork sets on loop-end blocks (PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp:746,867; PULPHardwareLoops.cpp:1598; SNITCHFrepLoops.cpp:561), so the lp.setup target label is not printed after reloading. -start-before=hwloopsfixup is unaffected (the pass re-sets the flag). Possible fix (owner decision): make the fork's AsmPrinter/passes derive the flag from lp.setup operands (e.g. mark every MBB used as an lp.setup/lp.setupi/frep target in a late pass or in RISCVAsmPrinter), or serialize the flag in MIR (upstream file edit). MIR tests that start after the fixup pass and check assembly are blocked by this; tests using -run-pass / -stop-after MIR checks are not.
proposed_test: llvm/test/CodeGen/RISCV/xpulp-hwloop-fixup-mir.mir: RUN: llc -mtriple=riscv32 -mattr=+xpulpv -run-pass=hwloopsfixup %s -o - | FileCheck %s, input = the -stop-before=hwloopsfixup MIR of xpulp-hwloop-countdown.ll, CHECK the LOOP0setup operand moved to the new split block and PseudoLOOPend; plus a RUN line with llc -stop-after=hwloopsfixup on an .ll (update_mir_test_checks.py) to cover registration of the name.
